newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: DAINONG, MIDOPA LIMIT UP ON FUND SUPPLY.
newsitem.headline: DAINONG, MIDOPA LIMIT UP ON FUND SUPPLY.

text.p: Shares of South Korea's Dainong Corp and Midopa Department Store went limit-up at the opening on Thursday on the news that emergency funds had been supplied to the two troubled companies, brokers said.
Dainong rose 190 won to 2,640 and Midopa gained 520 to 7,020.
"Investors are buying Dainong and Midopa shares following the news confirming rescue loans had been supplied," said Koh Soon-shik of LG Securities.
Brokers said the loan news should keep Dainong and Midopa shares firm for the rest of the day.

Dainong Corp received 5.7 billion won and Midopa 10.2 billion on Tuesday. The amount of the emergency loans was decided in late May after Midopa, Dainong and two other Dainong Group units were designated for a bail-out.
The funds were supplied after the group agreed to turn over management control to creditors.
